# TableView

Header: `winui/ui/collections/TableView.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/collections/TableView.hpp`.

A table: a header strip over virtualized rows, with sorting, resizable columns, frozen leading and trailing columns, four selection modes, cell templates, cell editing and collapsible groups.

Only the rows in view are realized, so a grid of 100,000 rows costs what a screenful does. Columns are fixed, Auto or fraction-sized ([TableViewColumnWidth](#struct-tableviewcolumnwidth)). When they are wider than the viewport, the table scrolls sideways with Shift+wheel, a horizontal wheel, Left and Right, or the horizontal scroll bar. Leading and trailing frozen columns stay in place. A click on a header sorts by that column through its [TableViewSortCycle](#tableviewsortcycle) and draws a chevron. Sorting reorders the table's own view of the rows, never [rows()](#rows), and the selection stays on the same rows. Dragging a header's trailing divider resizes the column between its min and max width.

A cell shows its text in [rows()](#rows) unless [set_cell_factory()](#set_cell_factory) builds an [Element](../tree/element.md) for it, such as a check box, a progress bar or an icon beside a caption. Those are built only for the rows in view and kept while their row stays in view or holds focus. They are children of the table, so they take pointer input and focus and screen readers see them. An Auto column measures them too, and the column still sorts by its text.

Editing is off until set_read_only(false). Then F2, or a double-click on a cell, opens an editor in the current cell. That is a [TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox) over a text cell, or what [set_cell_editor_factory()](#set_cell_editor_factory) builds, which is the only way to edit a template cell. Enter commits and Escape cancels. A press elsewhere in the table, or focus leaving it, commits. [on_cell_edited()](#on_cell_edited) sees every commit and can reject it, which keeps the editor open. While editing is possible, Left and Right move the current column instead of scrolling sideways, and scrolling follows it. The current column holds the cell F2 edits, ringed when focused.

[set_group_keys()](#set_group_keys) files the rows under collapsible group header rows, the groups in the order their keys first appear. A sort orders the rows within each group. A header row toggles on a click, Space or Enter. Left collapses it and Right expands it. Selection never lands on a header row, and it stays put while the columns scroll sideways.

The grid itself is the single tab stop. Up, Down, PageUp, PageDown, Home and End move through the rows and group headers in view order and scroll the row into view. Space selects in Single and Extended mode and toggles in Multiple mode. Shift extends a range in Multiple and Extended mode, and Ctrl moves without selecting there. Row indices everywhere in this API ([selected_row()](#selected_row), [selected_rows()](#selected_rows), [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed), [on_cell_edited()](#on_cell_edited)) are indices into [rows()](#rows), whatever the sort or grouping. Up from the first row moves onto the column headers. There Left and Right move between them, Enter or Space sorts, Ctrl+Left and Ctrl+Right narrow and widen the column, and Down goes back to the rows.

Example: 
```cpp
// Declarative: ui::TableView builds a ui::TableViewControl, one row per item.
using ui::operator""_fr;
struct Person { std::string name; std::string role; int years = 0; };
ui::Property<std::string> status{"Nothing selected"};
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{
    .spacing  = 8,
    .content  = {
        ui::TableView<Person>{
            .items   = {{"Ada Lovelace", "Engineer", 5},
                        {"Grace Hopper", "Architect", 12},
                        {"Alan Turing", "Researcher", 8}},
            .columns = {{.header = "Name", .width = 1_fr, .text = [](const Person& p) { return p.name; }},
                        {.header = "Role", .width = 160.0f, .text = [](const Person& p) { return p.role; }},
                        {.header  = "Years",
                         .width   = 80.0f,
                         .text    = [](const Person& p) { return std::to_string(p.years); },
                         .compare = [](const Person& a, const Person& b) { return a.years <=> b.years; }}},
            .height  = 240,
            .on_selection_changed = [&status](std::optional<Person> p)
            { status = p ? p->name + " selected" : "Nothing selected"; },
        },
        ui::Text{.text = status},
    },
});

// Imperative: the same control built by hand.
auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto grid  = std::make_unique<ui::TableViewControl>();
grid->set_columns({{.header = "Name", .width = 100.0f}, {.header = "Age", .width = 60.0f}});
grid->set_rows({{"Ada", "36"}, {"Grace", "85"}});
grid->on_selection_changed([&status](std::optional<std::size_t> row)
                           { status = row ? std::format("Row {}", *row) : ""; });
grid->set_selected_row(1); // fires the handler, scrolls row 1 into view
grid->sort_by_column(1, ui::TableViewSortDirection::Descending);
grid->set_read_only(false); // F2 or a double-click edits a cell
grid->on_cell_edited([](const ui::TableViewCellEditArgs& args)
                     { return args.text.empty() ? ui::Cancel : ui::Proceed; });
grid->set_group_keys({"Staff", "Guests"}); // one key per row
stack->add(std::move(grid));
```

## `ui::TableView`

A virtualized table: one row per item, one cell per column. Builds a [ui::TableViewControl](#uitableviewcontrol).

[`.items`](#uitableview-items) is the collection and takes the same sources as [ui::ListView](list-view.md#uilistview). Each column says which text it shows for an item, or gives a `cell` template that builds the cell's content from the item. Only visible rows are realized, so a large table costs what the viewport costs. When a bound collection changes, the rows are read again.

A header click sorts the table's view of the rows by that column, never [`.items`](#uitableview-items), and the selection stays on the same items. Dragging a header's divider resizes the column and reports it through [`.on_column_resized`](#uitableview-on_column_resized). Columns wider than the table scroll sideways, except frozen ones. Row indices ([`.selected_row`](#uitableview-selected_row), [`.selected_indices`](#uitableview-selected_indices)) are positions in [`.items`](#uitableview-items), whatever the sort or grouping. Nothing is selected until the user or [`.selected_row`](#uitableview-selected_row) picks a row.

[`.read_only = false`](#uitableview-read_only) lets the user edit cells with F2 or a double-click. Enter commits and Escape cancels. [`.on_cell_edited`](#uitableview-on_cell_edited) writes each value into its item or rejects it. [`.group_by`](#uitableview-group_by) files the rows under collapsible group headers.

Example: 
```cpp
struct Person
{
    std::string name;
    std::string role;
    int         years = 0;
    friend bool operator==(const Person&, const Person&) = default;
};
using ui::operator""_fr;
ui::Property<std::vector<Person>> people{{{"Ada Lovelace", "Engineer", 5}, {"Grace Hopper", "Architect", 12}}};
ui::Property<std::string>         status{};

window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{.content = {
    ui::TableView<Person>{
        .items   = people,
        .columns = {
            {.header = "Name", .width = 140.0f, .text = [](const Person& p) { return p.name; }, .frozen = true},
            {.header = "Role", .width = 1_fr, .text = [](const Person& p) { return p.role; }},
            {.header  = "Years",
             .width   = 80.0f,
             .text    = [](const Person& p) { return std::to_string(p.years); },
             .compare   = [](const Person& a, const Person& b) { return a.years <=> b.years; },
             .read_only = true},
        },
        .alternating_rows     = true,
        .read_only            = false,
        .group_by             = [](const Person& p) { return p.role; },
        .height               = 300.0f,
        .on_selection_changed = [&](std::optional<Person> p) { status = p ? p->name : ""; },
        .on_cell_edited       = [](const ui::TableViewCellEditedArgs<Person>& args)
        {
            if (args.text.empty())
            {
                return ui::Cancel; // keeps the editor open
            }
            (args.column == 0 ? args.item.name : args.item.role) = args.text;
            return ui::Proceed;
        },
        .empty_content        = ui::Text{.text = "No people yet"},
    },
    ui::Text{.text = status},
}});
```

Called with a copy of the selected row's item, the first in [`.items`](#uitableview-items) order under Multiple and Extended, or unset when nothing is selected (see [ui::SelectedItem](../tree/spec-vocabulary.md#selecteditem)). The copy is safe to keep. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_sorting"></span>`on_sorting` | `ui::Callback<ui::Decision(const ui::TableViewSortingArgs&)>` |  | Called with the column and the direction a header click or key is about to sort it in. Return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep the current order. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_sorted"></span>`on_sorted` | `ui::Callback<void(const ui::TableViewSortedArgs&)>` |  | Called with the column and its new direction after a sort change. The column is unset when the sort was cleared. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_column_resized"></span>`on_column_resized` | `ui::Callback<void(const ui::TableViewColumnResizedArgs&)>` |  | Called with the column and its new width in DIPs on every step of a user resize. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_beginning_edit"></span>`on_beginning_edit` | `ui::Callback<ui::Decision(const ui::TableViewBeginningEditArgs<std::type_identity_t<T>>&)>` |  | Called with the item and the column before an editor opens. Return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep it closed. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_cell_edited"></span>`on_cell_edited` | `ui::Callback<ui::Decision(const ui::TableViewCellEditedArgs<std::type_identity_t<T>>&)>` |  | Called on a commit with the item, the column and the editor's text. Write the value into the item and return [ui::Proceed](../core/namespace-ui.md#proceed) or nothing. Return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to reject it and keep the editor open. For a column with an `editing_cell`, `item` is the edited copy and the text is its cell text, and proceeding copies it into the collection. A [`ui::Property`](../core/property.md) collection is written back after an accepted edit. An [ObservableVector](../core/observable-vector.md)'s item is written back with [ObservableVector::replace()](../core/observable-vector.md#replace), so everything else showing it hears of the edit; an item that can't be copied is changed in place, without a notification. Without a handler a text edit only changes the cell as shown, until the rows are read again. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uitableview-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uitableview-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uitableview-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<std::type_identity_t<ui::TableView>>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. Its type uses std::type_identity_t, so passing a handle does not take part in deducing the type argument. |
| <span id="uitableview-empty_content"></span>`empty_content` | `ui::Spec` |  | Shown, centered in the body, while there are no rows. |
| <span id="uitableview-group_header_template"></span>`group_header_template` | `ui::Callback<ui::Spec(const std::string& key)>` |  | A group header's content from its key, shown after the chevron in place of the key and the count. Needs [`.group_by`](#uitableview-group_by). |
| <span id="uitableview-item_context_menu"></span>`item_context_menu` | `ui::Callback<std::vector<ui::MenuItem>(const std::type_identity_t<T>&)>` |  | The context menu of an item: a callable taking the item and returning the menu's entries. Called on a right-click on its row, or on Shift+F10 or the Menu key while it is current. The row is selected first. An empty list opens no menu. An item of a [ui::ObservableVector](../core/observable-vector.md) stays where it is while it is in the collection, so an entry's `on_click` may keep a reference to it. Any other item is valid during the call only, so capture it by value. |

### SortComparer

```cpp
using ui::TableViewControl::SortComparer = Callback<std::weak_ordering(std::size_t column, std::size_t row_a, std::size_t row_b)>
```

Orders two rows, by their indices into [rows()](#rows), for the column being sorted.

### CellFactory

```cpp
using ui::TableViewControl::CellFactory = Callback<std::unique_ptr<Element>(std::size_t row, std::size_t column)>
```

Builds the content of one cell, by its row (an index into [rows()](#rows)) and column. Returns nullptr to leave that cell as text.

### CellToolTip

```cpp
using ui::TableViewControl::CellToolTip = Callback<std::string(std::size_t row, std::size_t column) const>
```

The tip for a body cell, by its row (an index into [rows()](#rows)) and column. Empty means none, and the table's own [tool_tip()](../tree/element.md#tool_tip) shows instead.

### GroupHeaderFactory

```cpp
using ui::TableViewControl::GroupHeaderFactory = Callback<std::unique_ptr<Element>(std::size_t group)>
```

Builds the content of group `group`'s header row.

```cpp
const std::vector<std::vector<std::string>>& rows() const
```

The rows in source order. Each inner vector is one row's cell text, indexed by column. A row with fewer cells than there are columns shows blank cells past its own size.

### set_rows

```cpp
void set_rows(std::vector<std::vector<std::string>> rows)
```

Replaces every row, sorts them again by the current sort, clears the selection, and lays the table out again. Nothing is selected afterwards, in every selection mode. Raises [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed) when something was selected before.

### row_height

```cpp
float row_height() const
```

Height of every body row in DIPs; 40 by default. The header strip has its own fixed height of 40.

### set_row_height

```cpp
void set_row_height(float height)
```

Changes the row height, lays the table out again and rebuilds the visible rows.

### size_rows_to_content

```cpp
bool size_rows_to_content() const
```

Whether each row grows past [row_height()](#row_height) to fit its tallest cell. [Text](text.md#uitext) cells then wrap instead of being trimmed, and a template cell or an editor is measured at its own height. Off by default. A row keeps its height while it is out of view. Rows not yet seen count as [row_height()](#row_height) until they scroll in.

### set_size_rows_to_content

```cpp
void set_size_rows_to_content(bool on)
```

See [size_rows_to_content()](#size_rows_to_content).

### column_actual_width

```cpp
float column_actual_width(std::size_t column) const
```

The width the last arrange gave a column, whether it is fixed, Auto or a fraction. 0 before the first arrange or past the last column.

### set_column_width

```cpp
void set_column_width(std::size_t column, TableViewColumnWidth width)
```

Sets one column's width. A user resize does this, then raises [on_column_resized()](#on_column_resized).

### set_column_frozen

```cpp
void set_column_frozen(std::size_t column, bool frozen)
```

Pins one column, or lets it scroll again ([TableViewColumn::frozen](#struct-tableviewcolumn)). Keeps the sort.

### set_column_frozen_trailing

```cpp
void set_column_frozen_trailing(std::size_t column, bool frozen)
```

Pins one column against the right edge, or lets it scroll again ([TableViewColumn::frozen_trailing](#struct-tableviewcolumn)). Keeps the sort.

### can_user_resize_columns

```cpp
bool can_user_resize_columns() const
```

The table-wide switch for dragging header dividers; on by default. A column opts out with [TableViewColumn::can_resize](#struct-tableviewcolumn).


Called with the column and its new width in DIPs on every step of a user resize drag.


How far the columns are scrolled sideways, DIPs. 0 is the leading edge.

Scrolls sideways, clamped to how far the columns overflow the viewport, and redraws.

### can_user_sort_columns


The table-wide switch for sorting by a header click; on by default. A column opts out with [TableViewColumn::can_sort](#struct-tableviewcolumn).

### set_can_user_sort_columns

```cpp

```

See [can_user_sort_columns()](#can_user_sort_columns).


The sorted column. Unset while the rows are in source order.

### sort_direction


The sorted column's direction. None while unsorted.

### sort_by_column

```cpp

```

Sorts the view by `column` and clears any other column's sort. TableViewSortDirection::None restores the source order. The selected rows stay selected. Returns true when the sort changed, and then raises [on_sorted()](#on_sorted).

### toggle_sort_direction

```cpp
bool toggle_sort_direction(std::size_t column)
```

Does what a header click does: steps `column` to the next direction in its sort_cycle, unless [on_sorting()](#on_sorting) cancels. Returns true when the sort changed.

### header_cursor

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> header_cursor() const
```

The column header the keyboard is on. Unset while the keys move through the rows.

### clear_sort

```cpp

```

Restores the source order. Returns true when there was a sort to clear.

### set_sort_comparer

```cpp
void set_sort_comparer(SortComparer comparer)
```

Sets how two rows compare for a sort. Without one, the default, the cell text is compared, as numbers when both cells read as numbers ([compare_text()](#compare_text)).

### on_sorting

```cpp
void on_sorting(Callback<Decision(const TableViewSortingArgs&)> handler)
```

Called before a header click or key sorts a column. Return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep the current order. [sort_by_column()](#sort_by_column) does not raise it.

### on_sorted

```cpp
void on_sorted(Callback<void(const TableViewSortedArgs&)> handler)
```

Called after every sort change, with the column and its new direction. When the sort was cleared, the direction is None and there is no column.

### row_at_position


The index into [rows()](#rows) of the row shown at `position` in the sorted and grouped view. Unset for a group header and past the end.

### position_of_row


Where row `row`, an index into [rows()](#rows), is shown in the view. Unset while its group is collapsed.

### position_count


How many positions the view has: the rows shown plus the group header rows.

### selection_mode


The selection mode; Single by default. Switching to None clears the selection. Switching to Single keeps at most one row, the first selected.


See [selection_mode()](#selection_mode).

### selected_row

```cpp

```

The selected row with the lowest index into [rows()](#rows). Unset when nothing is selected.

### set_selected_row

```cpp
void set_selected_row(std::optional<std::size_t> index)
```

Selects `index` alone, clamped to the rows, and scrolls it into view. Does nothing, and fires no callback, if it is already the selection, if there are no rows, or under SelectionMode::None. Unset clears the selection.

### selected_rows

```cpp
const std::vector<std::size_t>& selected_rows() const
```

Every selected row, as ascending indices into [rows()](#rows).

### set_selected_rows

```cpp
void set_selected_rows(std::vector<std::size_t> rows)
```

Replaces the selection. Indices past the rows are dropped, Single keeps the lowest, None keeps nothing, and an empty list clears it. Raises [on_selection_changed()](#on_selection_changed) when the selection changed.

### is_row_selected

```cpp
bool is_row_selected(std::size_t row) const
```

Whether row `row`, an index into [rows()](#rows), is selected.

### on_selection_changed

```cpp
void on_selection_changed(Callback<void(std::optional<std::size_t>)> handler)
```

Called with [selected_row()](#selected_row) whenever the selection changes: by click, by key, by [set_selected_row()](#set_selected_row) or [set_selected_rows()](#set_selected_rows), or by [set_rows()](#set_rows) clearing a selection. Replaces any previous handler.

### set_item_context_menu

```cpp
void set_item_context_menu(Callback<std::vector<MenuItem>(std::size_t row)> menu)
```

Sets the context menu of row `row`, an index into [rows()](#rows). It is asked for on a right-click on the row, or on Shift+F10 or the Menu key while the row is the current one. The row is selected first, unless it already is or the selection mode is None. An empty list opens no menu. Replaces any previous one.

### raise_context_requested

```cpp
bool raise_context_requested(std::optional<Point> position) override
```

Opens the row's context menu ([set_item_context_menu()](#set_item_context_menu)) when no [on_context_requested()](../tree/element.md#on_context_requested) handler inside the row took the request.

### set_cell_factory

```cpp
void set_cell_factory(CellFactory factory)
```

Sets the cell factory. A cell it returns an [Element](../tree/element.md) for shows that [Element](../tree/element.md) instead of its text, stretched over the whole cell with no cell padding. Called once per cell as its row comes into view. The [Element](../tree/element.md) is kept while the row stays in view or holds focus, and built again after [set_rows()](#set_rows) or [set_columns()](#set_columns). Replacing the factory rebuilds every cell.

### set_cell_tool_tip

```cpp
void set_cell_tool_tip(CellToolTip tip)
```

Sets the per-cell tips; see [CellToolTip](#celltooltip).

### tool_tip_at

```cpp
std::string tool_tip_at(Point p) const override
```

The tip of the cell under `p` ([set_cell_tool_tip()](#set_cell_tool_tip)), else [tool_tip()](../tree/element.md#tool_tip).

### cell_element

```cpp
Element* cell_element(std::size_t row, std::size_t column) const
```

The [Element](../tree/element.md) a template cell shows while its row is in view. nullptr for a text cell or a row out of view.

### read_only

```cpp
bool read_only() const
```

Whether editing is off for the whole table, the default. A column opts out on its own with [TableViewColumn::read_only](#struct-tableviewcolumn).

### set_read_only

```cpp
void set_read_only(bool read_only)
```

Turns editing off or on. Turning it off commits an open edit, or cancels it when the commit is rejected.

### set_cell_editor_factory

```cpp
void set_cell_editor_factory(CellFactory factory)
```

Sets the factory for a cell's editor, by its row and column. Returning nullptr gives the default, a [TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox) over a text cell. A template cell without an editor is not editable. The editor is laid over the cell while the edit is open. The table stays the focused element and passes the keys and text on to the editor's first focusable control.

### is_editing

```cpp
bool is_editing() const
```

Whether a cell editor is open.

### editing_row

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> editing_row() const
```

The row of the open edit, an index into [rows()](#rows). Unset when none is open.

### editing_column

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> editing_column() const
```

The column of the open edit. Unset when none is open.

### editor

```cpp
Element* editor() const
```

The open editor, either the [TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox) or what the editor factory built, or nullptr.

### commit_edit

```cpp
bool commit_edit()
```

Closes the open edit and keeps its text. [on_cell_edited()](#on_cell_edited) runs first and may reject it. Returns false when nothing was open or the commit was rejected.

### cancel_edit

```cpp
bool cancel_edit()
```

Closes the open edit and leaves the cell as it was. Returns false when nothing was open.

### current_column

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> current_column() const
```

The current column, where a click on a cell or Left and Right put it. F2 edits its cell on the keyboard's row. Unset until then, and F2 then edits the first editable column.

### set_current_column

```cpp
void set_current_column(std::size_t column)
```

Moves the current column, clamped to the columns, and scrolls it into view.

### on_beginning_edit

```cpp
void on_beginning_edit(Callback<Decision(const TableViewCellArgs&)> handler)
```

Called before an editor opens on a cell, with its row and column. Return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to keep it closed.

### on_cell_edited

```cpp
void on_cell_edited(Callback<Decision(const TableViewCellEditArgs&)> handler)
```

Called on a commit with the cell and the editor's text. For an editor from the factory, the text is the cell's own text. Return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) to reject the value, which keeps the editor open. The handler may rewrite `text` to what the cell should show. Without a handler a commit stores the text in [rows()](#rows).

### set_cell_text

```cpp
void set_cell_text(std::size_t row, std::size_t column, std::string text)
```

Replaces one cell's text in [rows()](#rows) and redraws. The row keeps its place until the next sort.

### update_row

```cpp
void update_row(std::size_t row, std::vector<std::string> cells, std::optional<std::string> group_key = std::nullopt)
```

Replaces one row's text in [rows()](#rows), and its group key when [`group_key`](#group_key) is set, and builds its template cells again. The row keeps its place until the next sort, and an open cell editor stays open. A changed group key files the row under its new group.

### set_group_keys

```cpp
void set_group_keys(std::vector<std::string> keys)
```

Sets one key per row, by index into [rows()](#rows), the text its group header shows. Rows with the same key form a group. Groups follow the order their keys first appear in [rows()](#rows), and a sort orders the rows within each group. A collapsed group stays collapsed while its key is in use. An empty list, the default, shows the rows ungrouped. A row past the end of the list is filed under an empty key.

### set_group_header_factory

```cpp
void set_group_header_factory(GroupHeaderFactory factory)
```

Sets the group header content, shown after the chevron in place of the key and count. It is built for the headers in view only, and again when the groups change. A click on the row still toggles the group.

### group_header_element

```cpp
Element* group_header_element(std::size_t group) const
```

Group `group`'s built header content while its header is in view, else nullptr.

### group_keys

```cpp
const std::vector<std::string>& group_keys() const
```

The keys [set_group_keys()](#set_group_keys) was given.

### grouping_enabled

```cpp
bool grouping_enabled() const
```

Whether the keys group the rows; on by default. Off shows the rows ungrouped and keeps the keys, so turning it back on groups them again.

### set_grouping_enabled

```cpp
void set_grouping_enabled(bool enabled)
```

See [grouping_enabled()](#grouping_enabled).

### sticky_group_headers

```cpp
bool sticky_group_headers() const
```

Whether group headers are sticky; on by default. The current group's header stays pinned under the column headers until the next group's header pushes it up. A click on it still toggles the group.

### set_sticky_group_headers

```cpp
void set_sticky_group_headers(bool sticky)
```

See [sticky_group_headers()](#sticky_group_headers).

How many groups there are. 0 while the rows are not grouped.

How many rows a group holds, in or out of view. 0 past the last group.

Whether a group's rows are shown.

Row separators, column separators, both (the default) or neither.


Whether rows are banded: every second row in view order gets the alternating background. Off by default.


See [alternating_rows()](#alternating_rows).

Sets the banding color. Empty, the default, uses the theme's banding color.


See [set_alternating_row_background()](#set_alternating_row_background).

### set_empty_content


Sets what the body shows, centered, while there are no rows. nullptr, the default, shows nothing. The table owns it.

### empty_content

```cpp
Element* empty_content() const
```

The empty-state content, or nullptr.

### scroll_offset

```cpp
float scroll_offset() const
```

The body's current vertical scroll offset, DIPs.

### handle_shortcut

```cpp
bool handle_shortcut(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Handles the table's shortcuts. An Escape that closes a popup the editor opened, such as a [ComboBox](combo-box.md#uicombobox)'s list, leaves the edit open.

### cursor_at

```cpp
std::optional<CursorShape> cursor_at(Point p) const override
```

The resize cursor over a resizable header divider.

### focused

```cpp
bool focused() const
```

Whether the grid holds keyboard focus and draws its focus ring.

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

Focusable while enabled and holding at least one row.

### collect_focusables

```cpp
void collect_focusables(std::vector<Element*>& out) override
```

The table, then the focusable controls in its template cells and empty content. Never the editor, because the table keeps focus while one is open.

### for_each_child

```cpp
void for_each_child(ChildVisitor visit) const override
```

The table body, the empty-state content while it shows, the realized template cells and the open editor.

### automation_role

```cpp
AutomationRole automation_role() const override
```

Reported to screen readers as a data grid. It holds a header with one item per column, and invoking a sortable one sorts by it. Then come the rows in view, each selectable, and the group headers, which expand and collapse. A row holds its cells, one per column, each named by its text. A template cell's [Element](../tree/element.md) or an open editor sits under its cell. As in every virtualizing list, only the rows in view are reported.

### automation_children

```cpp
void automation_children(std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The empty-state content while it shows, the header, then the rows in view.

### automation_focus

```cpp
Element* automation_focus() const override
```

The row the keyboard is on, so a screen reader reads it as the arrow keys move.

### automation_parent_of

```cpp
Element* automation_parent_of(const Element& child) const override
```

The cell around a template cell or an open editor, and the header row around a group header's content, while their row is in view.

### compare_text

```cpp
static std::weak_ordering compare_text(const std::string& a, const std::string& b)
```

The default cell comparison. Compares as numbers when both texts parse entirely as numbers, else as text, ignoring ASCII case first.

### clear_dirty_override

```cpp
void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags) override
```

Clears the row context menu too, which is listed as a child only while it shows.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Desired size: the sum of the column widths, with fraction columns at their content width, by the header height plus every row. Each is clamped to `available` where it is bounded.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Resolves the column widths against the final width, splits the bounds into the header strip and the body, and arranges the body and the empty-state content.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the header strip, the realized rows, the grid lines, the scroll bars and the focus ring.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A press on a header sorts, or starts a resize on its trailing divider. A press on a body row selects it by the selection mode's rules.

### handled_pointer_override

```cpp
void handled_pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

A press a template cell took still commits an open edit elsewhere in the table.

### wheel_override

```cpp
bool wheel_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Vertical turns scroll the rows. Horizontal turns and Shift+wheel scroll the columns sideways when they overflow.

### hit_test_children

```cpp
void hit_test_children(Point p, std::vector<Element*>& out) const override
```

The children `p` (in this element's layout coordinates) is tested against, topmost first. Default: what [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) lists, last first. A container that draws in another order ([Panel](../layout/panel.md#uipanel)'s z-index), a control with parts [for_each_child()](#for_each_child) does not list, or one whose parts cover others in places (a pane drawn over the content) lists them here.

### covers_children_at

```cpp
bool covers_children_at(Point p) const override
```

Whether a part of this element drawn over its children is at `p` (a scroll bar over the content), so the element is hit there instead of a child. Default: false.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Ticks the children and the horizontal scroll bar's fade, and commits an edit whose focus left the table.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

The row keys described in the class comment. Left and Right scroll sideways, move the current column while editing is possible, or collapse and expand the group header the cursor is on. F2 opens an editor. While one is open, Enter commits, Escape cancels and every other key goes to the editor. Ignored while disabled or unfocused.

### text_override

```cpp
bool text_override(const TextInputEvent& text_event) override
```

Typed text goes to an open editor; without one it is ignored.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Called by [Window](../tree/window.md) as focus arrives or leaves. Redraws. An open editor follows the table's focus. Focus leaving commits the edit on the next tick unless it has come back by then.

### focus_ring_rect

```cpp
Rect focus_ring_rect(const Theme& theme) const override
```

Inside the header cell, group header, cell or row the keyboard is on, cut to the part in view. Around the whole table otherwise, and nowhere while an editor is open.

### focus_ring_corner_radius

```cpp
float focus_ring_corner_radius(const Theme& theme) const override
```

The ring's corner radius: the theme's control radius by default.

### focus_ring_inside

```cpp
bool focus_ring_inside() const override
```

Whether the ring goes inside [focus_ring_rect()](#focus_ring_rect) in every era, its outer edge on the rect. False by default, which leaves it to the theme. An item inside a viewport (a list row, a tab, a menu item) returns true, as does a control in a tight spot, so a neighbor or the viewport edge never cuts its ring.

## struct TableViewSortedArgs

What `on_sorted` gets after a sort change.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `column` | `std::optional<std::size_t>` |  | The sorted column; unset when cleared. |
| `direction` | `TableViewSortDirection` | `TableViewSortDirection::None` | Its new direction. |

## struct TableViewSortingArgs

What `on_sorting` gets before a user sort: the column and the direction it is about to take. Return [ui::Cancel](../core/namespace-ui.md#cancel) from the handler to keep the current order.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `column` | `std::size_t` | `0` | The column about to be sorted. |
| `direction` | `TableViewSortDirection` | `TableViewSortDirection::None` | The direction it is about to take. |

## struct TableViewColumnResizedArgs

What `on_column_resized` gets on every step of a user resize.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `column` | `std::size_t` | `0` | The resized column. |
| `width` | `float` | `0.0f` | Its new width, DIPs. |

## struct TableViewCellArgs

A [TableViewControl](#uitableviewcontrol)'s `on_beginning_edit`: the cell an editor is about to open on.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | `std::size_t` | `0` | An index into rows(). |
| `column` | `std::size_t` | `0` | The column. |

## struct TableViewCellEditArgs

A [TableViewControl](#uitableviewcontrol)'s `on_cell_edited`: the cell and the editor's text, which the handler may rewrite to what the cell should show.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `row` | `std::size_t` |  | An index into rows(). |
| `column` | `std::size_t` |  | The column. |
| `text` | `std::string&` |  | The editor's text. |

## struct TableViewBeginningEditArgs

```cpp
template <typename T> struct TableViewBeginningEditArgs
```

A [TableView](#uitableview) spec's `on_beginning_edit`: the item and the column an editor is about to open on.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | `T&` |  | The row's item. |
| `column` | `std::size_t` |  | The column. |

## struct TableViewCellEditedArgs

```cpp
template <typename T> struct TableViewCellEditedArgs
```

A [TableView](#uitableview) spec's `on_cell_edited`: the item, the column and the editor's text.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | `T&` |  | The row's item (the edited copy for an `editing_cell` column). |
| `column` | `std::size_t` |  | The column. |
| `text` | `const std::string&` |  | The editor's text. |

## struct TableViewColumnWidth

Derives from `ui::GridLength`.

A [TableView](#uitableview) column's width, in the same units as a [ui::Grid](../layout/grid.md#uigrid) track:

- Fixed DIPs: a plain number, or `120_dip` in a spec.
- Auto: [`ui::GridLength::auto_()`](../layout/grid.md#auto_), or [`ui::AutoSize`](../layout/grid.md#autosize) in a spec. As wide as its header and the cells in view.
- A fraction: [`ui::GridLength::fraction()`](../layout/grid.md#fraction), or `1_fr` in a spec. A weighted share of what the fixed and Auto columns leave of the viewport.

Converts implicitly from a number and from a [ui::GridLength](../layout/grid.md#struct-gridlength), so `{"Name", 140.0f}` and `{"Name", 1_fr}` both name a column.

### TableViewColumnWidth

```cpp
constexpr TableViewColumnWidth(float dips)
```

A fixed width of `dips`.

### TableViewColumnWidth

```cpp
constexpr TableViewColumnWidth(GridLength length)
```

Auto, a fraction or fixed DIPs, as `length` says.

## struct TableViewColumn

One column of a [TableView](#uitableview): its header, its width and how the user may size, sort and pin it.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | `std::string` |  | Caption drawn in the header strip above the rows. A caption too wide for the column is trimmed with an ellipsis, like the cells. |
| `width` | `TableViewColumnWidth` | `100.0f` | Fixed DIPs including the cell padding, Auto or a fraction; see [TableViewColumnWidth](#struct-tableviewcolumnwidth). [Cell](../layout/grid.md#uicell) text past the resolved width is trimmed with a trailing ellipsis. A user resize makes the column fixed at the width it was dragged to, and fixes the fraction columns before it at the widths they had, so only the columns after it give or take the room. |
| `min_width` | `float` | `20.0f` | The smallest and largest width, DIPs. The resolved width and a user resize stay inside them. |
| `max_width` | `float` | `Unbounded` | See [`min_width`](#struct-tableviewcolumn). |
| `can_resize` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the user can drag this column's header divider. The table's can_user_resize_columns() must be on too. |
| `can_sort` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a click on this header sorts by it. The table's can_user_sort_columns() must be on too. sort_by_column() works either way. |
| `sort_cycle` | `TableViewSortCycle` | `TableViewSortCycle::AscendingDescending` | The directions repeated header clicks step through. |
| `frozen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the column stays put while the others scroll sideways. Only a leading run of frozen columns is pinned. A frozen column after an unfrozen one scrolls. |
| `frozen_trailing` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the column stays put against the right edge while the others scroll sideways. Only a trailing run of such columns is pinned, and [`frozen`](#struct-tableviewcolumn) wins on a column that sets both. |
| `read_only` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the column's cells are never edited, even in a table that allows editing (TableViewControl::set_read_only(false)). A read-only column can still be the current one. |

## struct TableColumn

```cpp
template <typename T> struct TableColumn
```

One column of a [ui::TableView](#uitableview): its header, its width, the text it shows for an item, and how the user may size, sort and pin it.

The callables are std::function because columns are written as a braced list, which copies its entries.

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `header` | `std::string` |  | Caption drawn in the header strip above the rows. |
| `width` | `TableViewColumnWidth` | `100.0f` | A number of DIPs including the cell padding, [`ui::AutoSize`](../layout/grid.md#autosize) (as wide as the header and the cells in view) or a fraction (`1_fr`, `2_fr`: a weighted share of what the other columns leave). Header and cell text past the width is trimmed with an ellipsis. |
| `text` | `std::function<std::string(const T&)>` |  | The cell text for an item. |
| `min_width` | `float` | `20.0f` | The column's minimum and maximum width, DIPs. The resolved width and a user resize stay inside them. |
| `max_width` | `float` | `Unbounded` | See [`min_width`](#struct-tablecolumn). |
| `frozen` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the column stays put while the other columns scroll sideways. Only a leading run of frozen columns is pinned. |
| `frozen_trailing` | `bool` | `false` | Whether the column stays put against the right edge while the other columns scroll sideways. Only a trailing run of such columns is pinned. |
| `can_resize` | `bool` | `true` | Whether the user can drag this header's divider. The table's `.can_user_resize_columns` must be on too. |
| `can_sort` | `bool` | `true` | Whether a header click sorts by this column. The table's `.can_user_sort_columns` must be on too. |
| `sort_cycle` | `TableViewSortCycle` | `TableViewSortCycle::AscendingDescending` | The directions repeated header clicks step through. |
| `compare` | `std::function<std::weak_ordering(const T&, const T&)>` |  | How two items order for this column, for example `[](const T& a, const T& b) { return a.size <=> b.size; }`. Left out, the cell text is compared, as numbers when both cells are numbers. |
| `read_only` | `bool` | `false` | Whether this column is never edited, even in a table with [`.read_only = false`](#struct-tablecolumn). |
| `cell` | `std::function<Spec(T&)>` |  | The cell's content for an item, for example `[](Task& t) -> ui::Spec { return ui::CheckBox{.checked = t.done}; }`, stretched over the whole cell with no padding. Built for the rows in view only, and again when the collection changes. [`text`](#struct-tablecolumn) still sorts the column and names the cell. |
| `editing_cell` | `std::function<Spec(T&)>` |  | The editor for an item, shown over the cell while it is edited. It works on a copy of the item. A commit copies it back after `.on_cell_edited` accepts it, and a cancel drops it, so the item must be copyable. Without an editor, a text column edits in a [TextBox](text-box.md#uitextbox) and a column with a [`cell`](#struct-tablecolumn) template cannot be edited. |
| `tool_tip` | `std::function<std::string(const T&)>` |  | The tip shown while the pointer rests on the item's cell in this column, for example the full text of a trimmed cell. Empty for none. |

## Enumerations

### TableViewGridLinesVisibility

```cpp
enum class TableViewGridLinesVisibility
```

Which grid lines a [TableView](#uitableview) draws. Row banding is separate (set_alternating_rows()).

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `All` | Row separators and column separators (the default). |
| `Horizontal` | Row separators only. |
| `None` | No grid lines. |
| `Vertical` | Column separators only. |

### TableViewSortDirection

```cpp
enum class TableViewSortDirection
```

The direction a [TableView](#uitableview) column is sorted in.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `None` | Not sorted; the rows keep their source order. |
| `Ascending` | Smallest first; the header shows an up chevron. |
| `Descending` | Largest first; the header shows a down chevron. |

### TableViewSortCycle

```cpp
enum class TableViewSortCycle
```

The directions repeated clicks on a column header step through. An unsorted column starts at the first one named. The `*None` cycles end on unsorted, so a third click restores the source order.

| Value | |
| --- | --- |
| `AscendingDescending` | Ascending, Descending, Ascending, and so on (the default). |
| `AscendingDescendingNone` | Ascending, Descending, None. |
| `DescendingAscending` | Descending, Ascending, Descending, and so on. Suits metrics, largest first. |
| `DescendingAscendingNone` | Descending, Ascending, None. |
